view 1/ We kept losing YouTube videos to "title never mentions the topic." Here's the extraction ladder we shipped to fix it.
view 2/ The server runs on a datacenter IP. YouTube, Instagram and X all treat that as a bot after a few hundred requests.
view 3/ So the browser extension captures content client-side, on your own residential IP, already logged in.
view 4/ It grabs the rendered transcript panel, the DOM, the caption — whatever the site would show a real logged-in user.
view 5/ That gets POSTed to the server alongside the URL. No proxies, no stored cookies, no arms race.
view 6/ Server-side fallbacks still exist for when there's no extension capture — oEmbed, timedtext, OG tags.
view 7/ Every one of those fallbacks is allowed to fail. What's not allowed is failing silently.
view 8/ Every item records which rung of the ladder actually succeeded, and the UI shows it. Degradation is visible, always.
